podcast.title: Influence on Decline of Big Bands
podcast.body: The success of Louis Jordan and His Tympany Five, and their ability to produce a full sound with a smaller, cheaper lineup, contributed significantly to the decline of the big band era, as noted by Clarence "Gatemouth" Brown. "Clamants Gatemouth Vowl later claimed that Jordan had most of the responsibility for the decline of the big band, saying he could play just as good and just as loud with 5 or 17 and it was cheaper."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Pioneering "Jump Band Music" Sound
podcast.body: Louis Jordan's Tympany Five developed a unique sound, distinct from other contemporary bands, which became known as "jump band music." Their original lineup of Jordan plus five instruments (trumpet, sax, piano, bass, drums) managed to sound almost as full as larger big bands. "Jordan's new band had a sound, unlike anything else of the time."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
